# Inventory validation on 14 November 2026

**Executed locally on macOS.** The public source is a demonstration catalog. Every later mutation, outage and deletion was generated by the workload. The Azure deployment, access controls, cloud recovery and 60-second cloud freshness target still need a funded environment and an approved test run.

## Reproduce the recorded workload

Run the commands under **Run it** in the [README](../README.md) using a fresh database for each trial. The source adapter verified the two bounded HTTPS downloads against their pinned SHA-256 digests. Re-exporting yields 11,000 JSONL lines and SHA-256 `b3c8bf62b88d7d3c83b6321a50d54651523aecd0818e8af9c2b7a09b62e3ac15`. The cache and full export stay local. [Source revision, file sizes and license](SOURCE.md)

| Deterministic check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Initial state | 100 upstream sample products and 900 deterministic variants across three tenants |
| Source writes after seeding | 10,000 synthetic full-image mutations |
| Recovery interval | Consumer suspended from 1,200 to 1,800 seconds on the simulated clock. Source accepted 600 mutations, including four soft deletes, in that interval. |
| Restart | Reopened the database at the scheduled recovery poll. Applied 477 pending versions. All 1,000 current product images matched the independent input fold at recovery. |
| Durable current state | 1,000 keys, including 67 tombstones. All eight fields of each document matched the input-derived final state. SQLite integrity check passed. |
| Duplicate and stale replay | Re-delivered the latest version and an older seed version directly to the sink. Both preserved the final image. |
| Local audit grain | 9,784 applied mutation versions. 216 intermediate versions were coalesced. The 1,000 seed inserts are excluded. |
| Synthetic latency | 9,307 samples outside the recovery poll; 477 during recovery. Normal and full-run p95 both 14,000 ms. 416 versions exceeded 60 seconds. Maximum 614 seconds includes the interval since the last successful pre-outage poll. |
| SQL reports | 933 active products across three tenants. No outstanding deliveries and no quarantine records in the clean generated workload. Separate fault-injection fixtures exercise invalid and conflicting records. |

The standalone read-only verifier (`python3 verify_projection.py "$RUN_DIR/drill.sqlite" "$RUN_DIR/workload.jsonl"`) also reproduced the result and checked all 11,000 journal payloads and digests against the export. [Verification output](../examples/reconciliation.json)

An independent run folded the JSONL export by tenant and product and compared raw SQLite rows at recovery and completion. It reproduced all 1,000 images and the latency denominators. The audit is about versions the local sink applied. It does not measure the latency of intermediate changes that the feed coalesced. [Recorded drill output](../examples/drill.json)

## Actual local read visibility

The wall-clock timing trial submitted 1,000 mutations in batches of ten against a separately seeded database. A second SQLite connection read the committed projection after each batch. Nearest-rank p95 was **3.181 ms**, with a maximum of **4.223 ms**, across 1,000 visible versions. Each version in a batch shares the elapsed time for that batch. Timing starts immediately before source submission and ends after the target readback. Timing varies by machine. [Recorded timing output](../examples/local-timing.json)

## Cloud adapter checks exercised locally

The official Python SDK indexed the Function binding and retry metadata. Eleven offline tests exercised SDK document conversion, conditional Blob quarantine writes, Cosmos ETag races, SQL parameter binding, error propagation and dashboard HTML rendering. The transports and SQL cursor were local test doubles. The three container images and Azure service-to-service behavior require separate validation. [SDK test scope and commands](SDK_CHECKS.md)

Microsoft ScriptDom parsed the three Azure SQL scripts in Azure SQL grammar mode. All five batches and 17 top-level statements parsed without errors. See the [SQL validation record](SQL_VALIDATION.md) for the SDK versions, substitutions and commands.

## Test and build results

On 14 November, **36 distinct tests passed locally** using Python 3.14.7. The standard-library suite passed 25 tests (six source, nine engine, four integrated drill, three elapsed-outage and three cloud-contract tests). The pinned adapter suite passed 11 additional tests. GitHub Actions is configured to run on publication; these numbers come from local test runs.

```bash
python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -v
# Use the environment setup from docs/SDK_CHECKS.md
.venv/bin/python -m pip check
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s integration -p test_adapters.py -v
python3 infra/check_parameters.py --bicep "$HOME/.azure/bin/bicep"
```

Bicep CLI 0.46.1 compiled the template and development parameters with fixture values. The production-parameter control failed with the expected compiler error. The proposed lab and its pricing assumptions appear in the [budget worksheet](LAB_COST.md).

## Ten-minute outage on the local wall clock

In a separate run the consumer connection stayed closed for **600.016432 elapsed seconds** while a producer committed 600 individual updates, including four soft deletes. The maximum gap between submission starts was 1.010 seconds. Reopening and draining took 10.288 ms. All three cursors caught up and all 1,000 final product images matched the independent source fold. Of the 600 writes, 478 latest versions were applied and 122 coalesced. Among the 478 keys read after recovery, p95 time from submission to first independent verification was bounded above by 563.019 seconds. That clock includes the outage. [Run instructions](WALL_OUTAGE.md) · [Measured receipt](../examples/wall-outage.json)

## Publication verification on 18 November 2026

A fresh pinned public-source acquisition reproduced the 11,000-line workload and both committed reconciliation reports. All 1,000 product images matched. The initial GitHub adapter check found an incompatible Functions SDK pin for Python 3.12. Compatible per-runtime pins and a two-version adapter CI matrix corrected it. Isolated local Python 3.12.16 and 3.14.7 environments each passed the same 11 adapter tests, and Python 3.12.16 passed the 25 core tests. The distinct test count remains 36. [SDK compatibility details](SDK_CHECKS.md)
